enonce_intro_markdown:
**Topic 2**

Television is not good for children. Discuss.

questions.enonce_markdown: **Topic 2.** Discuss whether or not television is good for children. *(180 to 220 words)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Une consigne « Discuss » impose de présenter les deux faces d'une question (avantages puis inconvénients, ou l'inverse) avant de prendre position dans une conclusion personnelle motivée : un texte qui ne défend qu'un seul camp du début à la fin ne répond pas complètement à la consigne, même si chaque argument pris isolément est juste.

**Modèle de l'essai argumentatif (discuss) (180 à 220 mots) :**

Television has become a central part of many children's daily lives, and opinions are divided on whether this is beneficial or harmful.

On one hand, television offers children real advantages. Educational programmes teach reading, numbers, foreign languages and general knowledge in an entertaining way that keeps young minds engaged. Documentaries about nature, history and science broaden children's understanding of the world beyond their immediate environment, sometimes better than a textbook alone.

On the other hand, television carries real dangers for children. Many programmes contain violence, crime or adult content unsuitable for young viewers, and children who watch such content for hours often imitate the aggressive behaviour they see on screen. Excessive viewing also replaces time that should be spent reading, playing outdoors or doing homework, which can lower both academic performance and physical fitness. Furthermore, children exposed to constant advertisements develop materialistic desires their parents cannot always satisfy.

In my opinion, television itself is neither good nor bad; what matters is how it is used. Parents who select appropriate programmes, limit viewing time to one or two hours a day, and watch together with their children can turn television into a valuable educational tool rather than a harmful distraction. Television is therefore not inherently bad for children; poorly supervised television is.

### Piège à éviter
Se contenter d'empiler des arguments « pour » et « contre » sans jamais conclure personnellement laisse la question ouverte alors que le correcteur attend une position clairement assumée dans le dernier paragraphe.

### Conseil
Structure systématiquement un sujet « Discuss » en trois blocs visibles : un paragraphe « on one hand », un paragraphe « on the other hand », puis un paragraphe de conclusion personnelle introduit par « in my opinion » ou une formule équivalente.
